title: Two-dimensional arrays: tables of rows and columns

visuals.title: A 3 x 4 table: watch the loops visit every row and column to find the largest element
Match each word with its meaning

pairs.meaning: A horizontal line of elements. The FIRST index in m[i][j].
A vertical line of elements. The SECOND index in m[i][j].
The position number of a row or a column. It starts at 0.
One value of the table, for example m[1][2].
The way C++ stores a table in memory: the whole first row, then the second row, and so on.

goal: After this you can declare a 2-D array, fill it with nested braces, read and print it with nested loops, and calculate row sums and column sums.
warmup: Look at the result sheet pinned outside your classroom. Each row is one student and each column is one subject. To find Ali's mark in Maths you go to Ali's ROW and then to the Maths COLUMN. A cinema ticket works the same way: Row 3, Seat 5. A one-dimensional array is a single line of boxes. A two-dimensional array is a whole table of boxes, and you need TWO numbers to find a box.
definition: A 2-D array stores values in rows and columns, like a table or a matrix. It is declared with two sizes: type name[ROWS][COLUMNS]. int m[3][4] has 3 rows and 4 columns, so it holds 3 x 4 = 12 values. An element is reached with two indexes, m[row][column], and both indexes start at 0. So the first element is m[0][0] and the last one in int m[3][4] is m[2][3].
howItWorks: Think of the table with the row on the side and the column on top. m[1][2] means: go to row 1, then column 2. To visit every element we use two loops, one inside the other. The OUTER loop picks a row (i). For that row the INNER loop moves across all the columns (j). After the inner loop finishes, we print a new line and the outer loop moves to the next row. This is how input and output are done. Row sum: keep i fixed and let j change. Column sum: keep j fixed and let i change, so the outer loop is the column. Inside the computer memory is not a table but one long line. C++ stores the table row by row (row-major order): all of row 0, then all of row 1, and so on. That is why filling a table with cin fills the first row first.
syntax:
int m[3][4];                                  // 3 rows, 4 columns (rows first)
int t[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}};         // one inner {} per row
m[1][2] = 50;                                 // row 1, column 2 (counting from 0)
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {                 // outer loop: rows
    for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) {             // inner loop: columns
        cin >> m[i][j];                       // fills the table row by row
    }
}

The outer loop picks a row.
Reset the total for each new row. If this line were above the outer loop, totals would pile up across rows.
The inner loop walks across the columns of the chosen row.
i stays fixed (the row) while j changes (the column). Adds every element of row i.

The outer loop starts with row 0.
A fresh total for this row. It is created INSIDE the row loop, so it restarts at 0 for every row.
j = 2: add m[0][2] = 2. rowSum is 13. The inner loop ends.
Row 0 is finished, so print its total.
The outer loop moves to row 1.
rowSum is reset to 0 for the new row.

sample.title: Row sums, column sums and diagonal
sample.expectedOutput:
Row 0: 12
Row 1: 9
Row 2: 24
Column 0: 10
Column 1: 16
Column 2: 19
Diagonal: 13

explanation.text: Reads 9 numbers, filling the table ROW BY ROW: the first three go to row 0, and so on.
Row sums: the OUTER loop is the row i, the inner loop j walks across.
i is fixed (one row) while j changes.
Column sums: the loops swap roles. The OUTER loop is now the column j.
j is fixed (one column) while i walks down the rows. The element is still written m[i][j]: row first, column second.
The main diagonal has row = column: m[0][0], m[1][1], m[2][2]. One loop is enough.

variations.when: Two sizes in two pairs of brackets: rows first, then columns.
One inner pair of braces per row. This is the clearest way.
Also legal. The values fill the table row by row.
Start a table with every element 0.
The compiler counts the rows. The column count can NEVER be left out.
Two indexes, row first then column, both starting from 0.

variations.way: Read or print the whole table
variations.when: Nested loops: outer = rows (i), inner = columns (j).
Row sum: i fixed, j changes. Column sum: j fixed, i changes.

mistakes.error: error: declaration of 'm' as multidimensional array must have bounds for all dimensions except the first

No compiler error. The row loop must stop at the number of rows (3) and the column loop at the number of columns (4). With the bounds swapped, the program writes outside the array (undefined behaviour).

examTips: Say it as a rule: the first index is the ROW and the second index is the COLUMN. Write it in the margin before you start.
For a table with R rows and C columns the outer loop runs to R and the inner loop to C. Do not swap them.
A row sum needs a fresh total (set to 0) for each row, so declare it inside the outer loop. Check this in column sums too.
Show indexes in your trace: write m[1][2] = 7 and not just 7.
Remember that the last valid element is m[R-1][C-1]. Going outside the array gives no compiler error but wrong results.
romanSummary: 2-D array rows aur columns ki table hai. int m[3][4] ka matlab 3 rows aur 4 columns, yaani 12 elements.
Element m[row][col] se milta hai. Dono index 0 se shuru hote hain, pehle row phir column.
Input aur output ke liye nested loop lagta hai: bahar wala loop rows (i), andar wala loop columns (j).
Row sum mein i fixed rehta hai aur j badalta hai. Column sum mein j fixed aur i badalta hai.
Memory mein table row by row store hoti hai, aur har row ke baad cout << endl se nayi line shuru karte hain.

practice.prompt: How many elements does int m[3][4]; have?
practice.explanation: 3 rows with 4 columns each: 3 x 4 = 12 elements.

practice.prompt: Which element is the very first one of a 2-D array called m?
practice.hint: Indexes start from 0 in both directions.
practice.explanation: Both the row index and the column index start at 0.

practice.hint: The first index is the row, the second is the column.
practice.explanation: t[1][0] is row 1, column 0, which is 4. t[0][2] is row 0, column 2, which is 3.

practice.hint: m[i][i] has row = column. Which cells are those?
practice.explanation: The loop adds m[0][0] = 3, m[1][1] = 5 and m[2][2] = 5. That is the main diagonal and the total is 13.

practice.hint: The column index stays at 1. Which column is that?
practice.explanation: m[0][1] = 7 and m[1][1] = 1, so the loop adds the second column and prints 8.

practice.hint: The first size is the number of rows.
practice.explanation: The outer loop runs over rows, so it must stop at 3. The inner loop runs over columns, so it must stop at 4. The bounds were swapped.

practice.prompt: Write the code that declares int m[2][3] and reads its 6 elements from the keyboard, row by row.
practice.hint: Outer loop = rows, inner loop = columns.
practice.explanation: The outer loop goes through the 2 rows. For every row the inner loop reads the 3 columns, so the numbers fill the table row by row.

practice.prompt: How does C++ store int m[2][3] in memory?
options: Only the first row is stored
practice.explanation: Memory is one long line. C++ puts the whole first row, then the whole second row, and so on.

quiz.prompt: int marks[5][3]; means a table with
quiz.explanation: The first size is the number of rows and the second is the number of columns.

quiz.prompt: In m[i][j], what does j stand for?
quiz.explanation: In m[row][column] the first index picks the row and the second index picks the column.

quiz.prompt: To print a table row by row, which loop is the OUTER loop?
quiz.hint: Think of reading a page line by line.
quiz.explanation: The outer loop picks a row; the inner loop prints all columns of that row. Then cout << endl moves to the next line.

quiz.hint: Which size may be left out?
quiz.explanation: Only the row count may be omitted. The column count is always required.

quiz.prompt: In m[3][4], which element is the last one?
quiz.hint: Indexes stop one before the size.
quiz.explanation: Rows go 0 to 2 and columns go 0 to 3, so the last element is m[2][3].
